expectations.text: Rules are presented in groups of 3-5, not all at once
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows 5 groups: Group 1 (Code Style, rules 1-3), Group 2 (CSS, rules 4-6), Group 3 (Accessibility, rules 7-9), Group 4 (Performance, rules 10-12), Group 5 (Architecture, rules 13-15). Each group has exactly 3 rules.

expectations.text: Each group shows a table or list with rule, recommended tier, and reasoning
expectations.evidence: Each group has a markdown table with columns: #, Rule, Tier, Reasoning. E.g., Group 1 table shows 'No as any type assertions | T1 | Regex/lint can match as any...' for each rule.

expectations.text: At least 6 of the Code Style + CSS rules are correctly classified as T1
expectations.evidence: All 6 Code Style + CSS rules are classified as T1: as any (T1), export default (T1), nested ternary (T1), design tokens (T1), animation properties (T1), z-index tokens (T1).

expectations.text: The 'single responsibility' rule is classified as Human (inherently subjective)
expectations.evidence: Transcript Group 5: 'Components follow single responsibility principle | Human | SRP is inherently subjective. Explicitly listed as a Human example in the skill references.' Output file shows tier: Human.

expectations.text: The 'color alone does not convey meaning' rule is T3 visual-qa (requires visual inspection)
expectations.evidence: Transcript Group 3: 'Color alone does not convey meaning | T3 (visual-qa) | Requires visual judgment -- must look at rendered UI to determine if color is the sole differentiator.' Output file shows tier: T3 with agent: visual-qa.

expectations.text: Budget checks run after all blocks are generated
expectations.evidence: Transcript has a 'Budget Check (post-generation)' section at the end showing per-file breakdown and aggregated totals. Total T3: 7, Scopeless T3: 0, Critical T3: 0, all within limits.

expectations.text: The total rule count matches the actual number of rules in the file
expectations.evidence: Transcript states '15 rules classified' and Summary lists 8 T1 + 2 T2 + 4 T3 + 1 Human = 15. The output file contains exactly 15 enforcement blocks across all sections.

claims.claim: Existing T3 count is 3 (all in visual-rules.md)
claims.evidence: Cannot verify without reading the fixture's visual-rules.md, but consistent with eval-1 with_skill which made the same claim.

claims.evidence: Transcript Group 4 and Summary both document the gap: 'scoping to component files catches the structural violation but may flag legitimate event-handler localStorage use'.

eval_feedback.overall: Comprehensive eval for batch mode. The assertions cover grouping behavior, classification accuracy across tiers, budget checks, and rule counting. Good discriminating power.
